info.title: MICROSERVICE-development-fulfillment-dotnet-api-Delete Api Notification By Notification Id-v1-spec
info.description: The Notification Management API provides an efficient way for businesses to manage their notifications by allowing the deletion of specific notifications using their unique identifiers. This endpoint is essential for maintaining an organized notification system, enabling users to remove unwanted or outdated notifications seamlessly. Typical consumers include developers building applications that require dynamic notification handling, such as task management systems or event-driven architectures. The API ensures a clean interface for developers to integrate notification management efficiently.

delete.description: This endpoint allows you to delete a notification identified by its unique ID. Ensure that the notification you wish to delete exists before invoking this operation, as it will permanently remove the notification from the system.

id.description: The unique identifier of the notification.

endpoint.description: The endpoint associated with the notification.

protocol.description: The protocol used for the notification.

method.description: The HTTP method used for the request.

auth.description: Authentication method used for the notification.

received_bytes.description: The number of bytes received in the notification.

timestamp.description: Timestamp indicating when the notification was received.

data.description: The payload data of the notification.

DeleteApiNotificationByNotificationIdRes.description: Response object for the DELETE operation indicating successful deletion.

Date.description: The date and time when the response was generated, formatted in ISO 8601.

Server.description: The server software that is handling the request.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the response body, indicating the format of the returned content.

bearerAuth.description: This security scheme uses Bearer authentication, where the client must include a valid bearer token in the Authorization header of the request. The bearer token is usually obtained through an authentication process and serves to authenticate the user or application making the request.
